articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations on November 13, 2026, targeting individuals and entities involved in counter narcotics and counter terrorism activities.
These actions aim to disrupt financial networks supporting illicit drug trafficking and terrorist organizations globally.
Further details on the specific individuals and entities designated were provided by OFAC in their official announcement.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran Designation Update
body: OFAC released an update to its Iran designations on November 9, 2026, indicating further actions against entities and individuals connected to the Iranian regime.
This update is part of ongoing efforts to exert economic pressure on Iran.
The specific nature of the updated designations was detailed in the official OFAC announcement.

articles.headline: New Iran-Related Designations Announced by OFAC
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on November 6, 2026.
These designations target individuals and entities involved in activities supporting the Iranian government.
The action reinforces the U.S. government's commitment to countering Iran's destabilizing behavior.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Cyber-related and Transnational Criminal Organizations; Imposes Cuba Sanctions
body: On November 5, 2026, OFAC announced designations targeting cyber-related actors and transnational criminal organizations, alongside new sanctions against Cuba.
The actions aim to combat malicious cyber activities and disrupt criminal networks, while also addressing the Cuban government's actions.
A Cuba-related determination was also published as part of this comprehensive announcement.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Iran-Related Designations, Amends Venezuela General License
body: OFAC announced new Iran-related designations on November 4, 2026, along with updates to certain Iran-related listings.
An Iran-related OFAC Alert was also issued, and an amended Venezuela-related General License and Frequently Asked Question were published.
These measures reflect ongoing adjustments to U.S. sanctions policy concerning both Iran and Venezuela.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Iran-Related General License
body: On October 29, 2026, OFAC issued an amended Iran-related General License.
This amendment modifies existing authorizations concerning transactions involving Iran.
The specific changes and their implications are detailed in the official publication.

articles.region: North Korea / Democratic Republic of the Congo
articles.headline: OFAC Designates North Korea and Democratic Republic of the Congo Entities
body: OFAC announced new designations on October 28, 2026, targeting entities and individuals related to North Korea and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
These actions aim to counter proliferation financing from North Korea and address human rights abuses and corruption in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
The designations underscore the U.S. commitment to global security and human rights.

articles.headline: Extreme Networks, Inc. Reaches Settlement Agreement with OFAC
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a settlement agreement with Extreme Networks, Inc. on October 27, 2026.
The settlement resolves apparent violations of OFAC sanctions programs.
Details of the violations and the terms of the settlement were outlined in OFAC's public notice.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs on Blocking and Rejecting Transactions
body: On October 26, 2026, OFAC issued amended Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) regarding blocking and rejecting transactions and filing reports with OFAC.
These amendments provide updated guidance for financial institutions and other entities on their compliance obligations.
The revised FAQs aim to clarify reporting requirements and procedures for handling sanctioned transactions.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran-Related Designations, Belarus and North Korea Removals, and New General Licenses
body: OFAC announced new Iran-related designations on October 21, 2026, alongside removals of certain Belarus and North Korea designations.
The agency also issued new Iran-related and Russia-related General Licenses and amended Frequently Asked Questions.
This multifaceted action reflects a dynamic approach to sanctions policy across several key regions.

articles.headline: UK Updates Sanctions List for Democratic People's Republic of Korea
body: On November 17, 2026, the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office updated the UK Sanctions List with a variation concerning the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK) regime.

The update specifically relates to the Mansudae Overseas Project Group of Companies, also known as Mansudae Art Studio, which is involved in exporting DPRK workers for construction activities to generate revenue for the DPRK government.

The entity remains subject to an asset freeze, chartering of ships, closure of representative offices, crew servicing of ships and aircraft, prevention of business arrangements, and prohibition of port entry.

articles.headline: UN Security Council Renews Yemen Sanctions Regime Against Houthis
body: The UN Security Council unanimously renewed its Yemen sanctions regime on November 12, 2026, extending targeted asset freezes, travel bans, and arms embargo enforcement measures for 12 months.
The resolution, 2837 (2026), strongly condemns the military escalation by the Houthis and demands an immediate cessation of their military actions and attacks.

The renewed framework includes enhanced restrictions targeting components and chemicals used in Houthi drone and missile manufacturing, and expands the UN panel monitoring sanctions to include maritime-security expertise.
articles.source: UN Meetings Coverage and Press Releases / Gulf News

articles.headline: UN Security Council Committee Amends North Korea Sanctions List Entry
body: On November 13, 2026, the United Nations Security Council Committee established pursuant to resolution 1718 (2006) amended one entry on its sanctions list.

The amendment pertains to the Mansudae Overseas Project Group of Companies, also known as Mansudae Art Studio, which is involved in generating revenue for the Government of the DPRK through the exportation of workers.
This action reflects ongoing efforts to refine and update the UN's sanctions against North Korea.
articles.source: UN Security Council / Financial Intelligence Unit

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.
